Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strengthened: BOCRA's 2024 Annual Report records 97% population 4G coverage as of March 2024 (up 1.2pp, target 100% of gazetted settlements by 2029), and Internet Society Pulse reports 99% 4G coverage. Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DataReportal's 77.3% (Jan 2024) figure is corroborated by a November 2025 Africa-Press article citing a fresher DataReportal estimate of 81.4% penetration, and by Statistics Botswana's 2024 household ICT survey (68.9% household internet access, rising trend). One outlier estimate (Internet Society Pulse, ~57%) was not corroborated elsewhere. Weight of evidence supports 70%+, so score 5 is confirmed.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
Comments: ~85% unique subscribers est from 172% connections [GSMA via DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2024-botswana)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original score relied on an estimate derived from GSMA connections data (172.8% of population, i.e. SIM/connections, not unique subscribers). Statistics Botswana's 2024 Household Access and Individual Use of ICTs survey provides a direct, authoritative figure: 84.2% of the population (aged 5+) used a mobile telephone in 2024. This independently confirms the 70%+ band with much stronger evidence; score 5 confirmed.

Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The claimed 94% smartphone-connections figure could not be verified — the cited DataReportal page, read in full, does not contain this statistic. Statistics Botswana's 2024 household ICT survey found smartphones present in 537,435 of 753,862 households (71.3%), and GSMA's 2025 Sub-Saharan Africa smartphone report puts the regional average share of connections at only 42-63% (2023-2025), well below 94%. Downgraded from 5 to 4 (60-79% band) using the household survey as the best verified proxy; flagged for human review given the metric mismatch (device ownership vs. connections share) and the unverifiable original claim.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Value Name: Comprehensive requirements for personal data or broad categories
Comments: Soft requirement to retain copy of personal data in country [TechHive](https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/understanding-botswanas-new-data-protection-act-key-updates-and-changes)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a second source: Botswana's Data Protection Act 2024 (in force 14 Jan 2025) restricts cross-border transfer of personal data under Section 74 unless adequacy or other conditions are met, applying broadly to personal data rather than one sector. This supports 'comprehensive requirements for personal data' (4), though it is a transfer-restriction mechanism rather than an explicit in-country storage mandate; flagged for human review given this nuance in interpretation.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Downgraded from 3 to 2. The original World Bank PDF cited was a 2023 project-concept document (not evidence of an existing framework). The World Bank's National Energy Compact for Botswana (2025/26) states explicitly there is 'no clear regulatory framework for mini-grids', with licensing, tariff-setting and grid-arrival policy still undefined, and commits to developing 'national technical standards, policies and framework' only by 2026. Current deployment is limited to a handful of pilot villages and 2020 Rooftop Solar Guidelines. This matches 'basic policy exists but limited implementation' (2) rather than an active, established policy.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.

Afrobarometer's 2024 finding that only about half of Batswana have reliable electricity corroborates. Score of 2 confirmed.
